title: Characterisation of the Last Previous Visit
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $n,t,s\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\tau$ be a work-tape index. If the last time before step $t$ at which tape $\tau$'s head occupies its position at step $t$ is $s$, then $s<t$, the head positions at steps $s$ and $t$ agree, and at every step $r$ with $s<r<t$ the head position differs from its position at step $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state binary Turing machine
The last previous visit at time $t$ is $s$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$,
let $n, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\tau \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, and for $s \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$w(s)$ be the position of the head of work tape $\tau$ after $s$ steps of $M$ on the
all-zeros input $0^n$, and let $\mathrm{prev}$ be the largest $s < t$ with $w(s) = w(t)$,
undefined when there is no such $s$. If $\mathrm{prev}$ is defined and equals $s$, then
$s < t$, $w(s) = w(t)$, and $w(r) \ne w(t)$ for every $r$ with $s < r < t$.
